cr-0DSE.title: Stadium: surrounded by dark blue walls
cr-0DSE.summary: A stadium in southern Cartago can be recognised by the dark blue walls around it.

cr-0aiX.title: Trees: teak with tall trunks
cr-0aiX.summary: Teak has tall straight trunks and round, glossy, yellow-green leaves, and is most common in Guanacaste.

cr-1FnG.title: Houses: pastel concrete, fences, barred windows
cr-1FnG.summary: Pastel-coloured concrete houses, low single-family homes or boxy two-storey ones, with dark red metal or plastic roofs. Heavy fences and barred windows can hide the buildings. Less colonial than Panama.

differs.how: More colonial style, with tiled roofs

cr-1dUl.title: Taxis: red with yellow triangles
cr-1dUl.summary: Taxis are red with yellow triangles on the sides and roof showing the town name and a letter code for the province.

cr-2XHK.title: Coverage: white building with round windows
cr-2XHK.summary: In Liberia, a white building with rounded windows and brown wooden frames appears in all the coverage.

cr-3jYU.title: Pole: white plate with black letters
cr-3jYU.summary: White pole plates with black lettering are specific to the Greater Metropolitan Area. They are usually held on by metal bands, though sometimes missing.

cr-4854.title: Coverage: city streets in a few places
cr-4854.summary: City coverage is mainly in and around San José and Cartago, but also Liberia and Filadelfia.

cr-4La3.title: Houses: on stilts, northeast coast
cr-4La3.summary: Houses raised on stilts are mostly found on the northeastern coast.

cr-4M9N.title: Google car: antenna folded down
cr-4M9N.summary: The antenna is occasionally folded down, mostly in the north and northeast.

cr-4iGB.title: Pole: low even crossbar, 2+1 insulators
cr-4iGB.summary: A common pole top has an even crossbar sitting low on the pole, with one insulator on one side and two on the other. Costa Rican poles usually have support bars. Panama's rarely do.

differs.how: Panamanian poles rarely have support bars

cr-64Q4.title: Palms: round crown, messy bunches, spiky trunk
cr-64Q4.summary: Macaw palms are common in the west, with long, messy-looking leaf clusters forming a nearly round crown and usually a spiky trunk.

cr-7Mg2.title: Fences: rough wooden branch or log fences
cr-7Mg2.summary: Simple fences made of irregular branches or logs are found everywhere but much more in the west. Elsewhere, planted tree rows or spiked concrete fences are more common.

cr-8lrg.title: Pole: tall yellow paint, 3 numbered sections
cr-8lrg.summary: Tall yellow pole paint divided into three sections with numbers, mainly in Puntarenas and southern Alajuela.

cr-9Slh.title: Coverage: late evening and night shots
cr-9Slh.summary: Late evening and night coverage is found in the southern town of San Vito.

cr-9TUK.title: Pole: single insulator on the side at the top
cr-9TUK.summary: Poles with a single insulator fixed to the side near the top are common.

cr-AMIc.title: Fields: rice paddies with raised edges
cr-AMIc.summary: Rice fields are mostly south of Bagaces in Guanacaste. Even harvested or newly planted ones show raised edges around the paddies.

cr-AOrt.title: City: valley, inclines, taller buildings
cr-AOrt.summary: The capital sits in a valley between mountains, so roads climb and dip. You see lots of suburbs and the tallest buildings in the country.

cr-ATZk.title: Plants: banana plantations in the east
cr-ATZk.summary: Most banana plantations are in Limón province in the east. Wild bananas and garden bananas are found almost everywhere.

cr-B7ks.title: Pole: small black stickers with a QR code
cr-B7ks.summary: Small black stickers with a QR code at the bottom appear around Corralillo, south of San José.

cr-CAr4.title: Road: sugarcane and dracaena along the roadside
cr-CAr4.summary: In a recreation park southwest of Poás, a road is lined with sugarcane plantations and cornstalk dracaena plants.

cr-DdPx.title: Gate: big orange wooden gate at park entrance
cr-DdPx.summary: At the entrance to Laguna de Fraijanes park, a large orange wooden gate separates the road from a car park. The park surrounds a small lagoon.

cr-EymR.title: Pole: one insulator one side, two on the other
cr-EymR.summary: Poles with one insulator on one side and two on the other are found around the capital. Poles with all insulators on one side are found across the country.

cr-FAHB.title: Pole: yellow paint, 2 sections
cr-FAHB.summary: Yellow pole paint in two sections with horizontal characters at the bottom is almost only found in southern Alajuela. Two sections without the horizontal characters are found almost everywhere.

cr-GPIi.title: Museum: palace-like front with a street railway
cr-GPIi.summary: The Cartago Municipal Museum has a palace-like facade, a neat garden in front, and a railway in the middle of the street.

cr-GaPT.title: Vehicles: tuk-tuks on the coast
cr-GaPT.summary: Tuk-tuks are seen around Puerto Viejo de Talamanca on the northeast coast, and less often around Nosara on the west coast.

cr-Gv5P.title: Stadium: boxy, red, blue and white
cr-Gv5P.summary: A stadium in Heredia, northwest of San José, with a boxy shape and a red, blue and white colour scheme.

cr-H7Rf.title: Google car: Gen 3 only backpacks and a boat
cr-H7Rf.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage is very limited: backpack walks around the capital and the northern west coast, Cocos Island, and a boat near Caño Island.

cr-Hh2x.title: Coverage: dry-season shots in the west
cr-Hh2x.summary: A lot of the western coverage was taken in the dry season, so it looks drier and browner.

cr-I3Ot.title: Pole: lamp with a blue dot on top
cr-I3Ot.summary: Utility poles carry a lamp with a blue dot on the top, as in Panama, Colombia and Brazil.

cr-I7Hg.title: Resort: red brick paving of Turkish shape
cr-I7Hg.summary: The Punta Leona Resort, near the Playa Mantas POI, has red brick paving with bricks shaped like those common in Turkey.

cr-J1g1.title: Coverage: park edge with L-shaped red bricks
cr-J1g1.summary: Most of the coverage in Filadelfia de Guanacaste is at the edge of a park, with red brick paving laid in L shapes.

cr-K2iz.title: Sign back: cross brace behind warning signs
cr-K2iz.summary: Many road signs have a distinct cross on the back, most often on diamond warning signs. Colombia almost always has the cross, but on white posts.

differs.how: Cross on almost every sign, with white signposts

cr-KYKK.title: Bollard: orange board with 3 black circles
cr-KYKK.summary: Instead of bollards, look for vertical orange boards with three black circles.

cr-NRyJ.title: Pole: thin metal crossbar bent into an L
cr-NRyJ.summary: A thin metal crossbar bent 90 degrees into an L shape is common. Panama, Colombia and Ecuador have it too, but crossbars are less common in Panama.

cr-NyKR.title: Park: large park with sports facilities
cr-NyKR.summary: La Sabana Park has several sports facilities, including the National Stadium, in its western part.

cr-O51t.title: Flags: each province has its own flag
cr-O51t.summary: Every province has its own flag, which you may see on buildings.

cr-OMhy.title: Provinces: names sometimes on signs
cr-OMhy.summary: Province names are sometimes written on signs, so it helps to know them.

cr-RSDA.title: Pole: short yellow paint
cr-RSDA.summary: Shorter yellow pole paint with all the numbers and no dividing lines, mainly in Guanacaste and northwestern Alajuela.

cr-RSLp.title: Pole: numbers made of wire
cr-RSLp.summary: Pole attachments shaped like numbers made of wire are found in central Alajuela and over the border in Heredia.

cr-Rg9U.title: Follow car: yellow with two front windows
cr-Rg9U.summary: A yellow follow car with two front windows trails the Google truck on RN 2 east of Palmar Norte, halfway to Buenos Aires. The river valley is also distinctive.

cr-RsZ0.title: Street sign: green with a white emblem box
cr-RsZ0.summary: The capital municipality consistently uses green street signs with a white rectangle holding an emblem. Calle and Avenida numbers increase from downtown outwards.

cr-SD0q.title: Pole: large black or white stickers with numbers
cr-SD0q.summary: Poles sometimes carry big black or white stickers with several lines of text. The first digit of the top number tells you the province.

cr-TnhG.title: Landmark: museum with a castle-like exterior
cr-TnhG.summary: The Children's Museum in northern San José has a grand, castle-like building.

cr-Vms6.title: Railways: only a few lines
cr-Vms6.summary: There are only a few train tracks: some in the Greater Metropolitan Area, one to the west coast, and one east through Turrialba to Siquirres, continuing to Limón and the northwest.

cr-VtdW.title: Palms: upward leaves that droop slightly
cr-VtdW.summary: Attalea palms have upward-pointing leaves that droop a little. They grow mainly along the southern coast.

cr-WEnx.title: Plants: pineapple plantations
cr-WEnx.summary: Pineapple plantations are in western Limón, northern Alajuela, and around Buenos Aires in Puntarenas.

cr-Y5zz.title: Plants: coffee plantations in the central valley
cr-Y5zz.summary: Most coffee plantations are throughout the central valley.

cr-Z9ea.title: Ruins: remains of a large church
cr-Z9ea.summary: The Ruins of Cartago are the remains of a large Catholic church near the city centre, and one of the first things to show up when you zoom into the city.

cr-aI96.title: Backpack: downhill stair trail to a waterfall
cr-aI96.summary: Near La Fortuna, a Gen 4 backpack walk goes down a trail with many stairs to a waterfall, with a brown-haired walker and a camera crew. Another trail at a nearby park has a black-haired walker.

cr-adoV.title: Canals: large irrigation canals
cr-adoV.summary: Larger irrigation canals are found south of Bagaces and Cañas in Guanacaste province.

cr-dq4a.title: Electricity meter: round, big metal box beside
cr-dq4a.summary: Round electricity meters, often with a large metal box next to them. Mexico and other North American countries have round meters too.

cr-dyRW.title: Landscape: lush hills, volcanoes, rainforest
cr-dyRW.summary: A lush tropical country with rolling hills, farmland lowlands, pointed volcanoes through the middle and patches of dense rainforest.

cr-fu5H.title: Rocks: dark volcanic rocks
cr-fu5H.summary: Dark volcanic rocks are found in much of central Costa Rica, and more so around Guápiles in Limón and around the Miravalles Volcano.

cr-gNL6.title: Taxis: red
cr-gNL6.summary: Red taxis are the standard. Panama uses yellow taxis.

cr-gPNt.title: Landscape: flat lowlands, grey dirt
cr-gPNt.summary: North of the mountains the Caribbean lowlands are largely flat, with lots of farming, grey dirt and straight roads. Overcast is common but some places are sunny.

cr-gRxp.title: Plants: cassava plantations in the east
cr-gRxp.summary: Cassava plantations are most common in western Limón province.

cr-gTTP.title: Campus: busy, green, medium buildings
cr-gTTP.summary: The University of Costa Rica in eastern San José is busy and green, with many medium-sized buildings across the campus.

cr-gY25.title: Landmark: wealthy homes and a small tower
cr-gY25.summary: Around the National Museum you see several wealthy-looking homes and a small tower like those on medieval European fortresses.

cr-gY2v.title: Ads: beer with black eagle mascot
cr-gY2v.summary: Ads for a beer with a black eagle mascot are common.

cr-h0O1.title: Campus: mountain range to the south and east
cr-h0O1.summary: The Costa Rica Institute of Technology usually shows a mountain range to the south and east.

cr-h4cR.title: Sign: stop sign says ALTO
cr-h4cR.summary: Stop signs say ALTO, as in Mexico, Panama and Guatemala. The rest of Spanish-speaking Latin America writes PARE. Panama's ALTO has a thicker font.

cr-hidd.title: Pole: blue P-XXXXX code
cr-hidd.summary: Blue lettering forming a P-XXXXX code, with or without a white background, is found in western Cartago province.

cr-iRIo.title: Pole: long silver insulators
cr-iRIo.summary: Poles carry long silver insulators. Panama has these among other kinds, and Brazil can have them too, while Ecuador uses UFO and mushroom ones.

cr-iWum.title: Language: Spanish
cr-iWum.summary: Spanish is the language, as in most of Latin America. Brazil speaks Portuguese.

cr-iZh4.title: Landmark: orange footbridge over a highway
cr-iZh4.summary: An orange pedestrian bridge crosses a major highway at Parque de la Paz in southeastern San José.

cr-j1NK.title: Plants: sugarcane, silvery tufts in the south
cr-j1NK.summary: Sugarcane is grown in several areas. In the south, around San Isidro de El General and Buenos Aires, it often flowers with silvery tufts on top.

cr-jFoY.title: Bollard: yellow, between the centre lines
cr-jFoY.summary: From the Route 32 toll near the San José and Heredia border to the junction with RN 4 west of Guápiles, yellow bollards sit between the centre lines.

cr-jSmB.title: Garden: bad dirt road, mountains, curvy paths
cr-jSmB.summary: At the entrance of the Lankester botanical garden, southeast of Cartago, a poorly kept dirt road runs with mountains in the distance and a name sign. Inside, walkways curve softly and are almost never straight.

cr-kDJo.title: Highways: only two concrete stretches
cr-kDJo.summary: The only concrete highways are the eastern stretch of Ruta 18 and the divided Pan-American Highway (Ruta 1) from Liberia to Ruta 18.

cr-m8UD.title: Plate: short, white, blue text
cr-m8UD.summary: Plates are short and white with blue text, which gives a light blue tint through the blur. This helps tell it apart from Panama.

differs.how: Panamanian plates are not tinted light blue

cr-mSOa.title: Plants: oil palm plantations on the coast
cr-mSOa.summary: Most oil palm plantations are along the coast of Puntarenas province, with a few smaller ones in Limón. Single oil palms appear all over, especially on the east coast.

cr-nIlI.title: Coverage: forest backpack walks in the middle
cr-nIlI.summary: Most rural forest backpack walks are in central Costa Rica. Cocos Island is mainly dense tropical forest too.

cr-nmwZ.title: Coverage: beach backpack walks
cr-nmwZ.summary: Beach backpack walks are mostly on the northern west coast, but also west of San José and on Cocos Island.

cr-q9ep.title: Coverage: three dogs follow in pine forest
cr-q9ep.summary: In a recreation centre just east of San José de la Montaña, three dogs follow the backpack through a pine forest.

cr-sTF8.title: Google car: white pickup, front antenna
cr-sTF8.summary: A large white pickup truck with an antenna on the front, often partly visible but sometimes fully blurred. Panama's truck is almost always fully blurred, and Ecuador's has no antenna.

differs.how: Truck is almost always fully blurred

cr-sUXT.title: Filming crew: black Toyota with camera crew
cr-sUXT.summary: A well-known streamer, or his film crew on top of a black Toyota, can be spotted around La Fortuna in Alajuela.

cr-yCjN.title: Trees: thick trunk, big umbrella crown
cr-yCjN.summary: Guanacaste trees have thick trunks and a large umbrella-shaped crown. They are mostly seen in Guanacaste province.

cr-yFUc.title: Landmarks: wind turbine clusters
cr-yFUc.summary: Wind turbines stand in a few clusters, mainly in Guanacaste (La Fortuna, Tilarán, Santa Cruz, north of Liberia) and southwest of Cartago.

cr-ylQi.title: Phone numbers: area codes moderately useful
cr-ylQi.summary: Area codes help a bit with locating a round. Worth learning if you want extra detail.

cr-zTr2.title: Highway: divided road through lush flat forest
cr-zTr2.summary: The RN 32 is a major divided highway from the junction with RN 4 to Limón on the Caribbean coast, through lush forests in the flat northern lowlands. Other divided highways are near the capital.

cr-zf4y.title: Pole: black sticker, yellow letters, low
cr-zf4y.summary: Black pole stickers with yellow lettering, low on the pole, are only in western Guanacaste and the Nicoya peninsula.

cr-zp0y.title: Road: bright white soil
cr-zp0y.summary: Roads with bright white soil probably put you just north of Liberia in Guanacaste.

cr-zwKu.title: Coverage: backpack on a four-lane road
cr-zwKu.summary: At the main airport the backpack walks in the middle of a big four-lane road. There is also coverage just outside the terminal.
